summary: A dc-voltage-biased SQUID couples a high-Q memory resonator to a lossy buffer mode, engineering single-, two-, and four-photon dissipation through dynamical Coulomb blockade where the energy $2eV$ from Cooper pair tunneling matches multi-photon transitions. The approach suppresses parasitic nonlinearities by construction compared to parametrically pumped couplers, with measured two-photon loss rate $\kappa_2/2\pi = 0.51$ MHz and maximum two-to-one coupling $g_2^{\mathrm{max}}/2\pi = 18.5 \pm 0.5$ MHz.
motivation: Multi-photon dissipation is essential for stabilizing bosonic qubits like cat qubits, but conventional parametric couplers suffer from spurious Kerr and cross-Kerr terms that limit performance at large pump power. dc-voltage-biased junctions offer an alternative where these parasitic terms rotate at the Josephson frequency $\omega_J = 2eV/\hbar$ and average to zero by construction.
method: A SQUID with tunable $E_J/h$ up to 13 GHz was coupled galvanically to memory ($\omega_a/2\pi = 4.04$ GHz, $T_1 = 3.1$ µs) and buffer ($\omega_b/2\pi = 7.56$ GHz, $\kappa_b/2\pi = 85$ MHz) resonators via stepped-impedance filtering; matching $2eV = n\hbar\omega_a - \hbar\omega_b$ activated $n$-to-1 photon swaps, characterized by Wigner tomography using a dispersively coupled transmon ($\chi/2\pi = 1.51$ MHz).
result: Two-photon dissipation was demonstrated with adiabatic-elimination model matching observations at low $E_J$ ($\kappa_2 = 4g_2^2/\kappa_b$), reaching $\kappa_2/2\pi \approx 0.5$ MHz; spurious one-photon loss and dephasing scaled as $E_J^2$, attributed to environmental modes at $\omega_a \pm \omega_J$ and requiring improved impedance filtering to suppress by $\sim 3$ orders of magnitude for viable cat-qubit stabilization.
